title: I Swapped the Shared Fridge Labels After My Lunch Kept Vanishing

parts.text: I opened the office fridge at 12:07 and my blue Tupperware was gone again. The shelf still smelled like leftover garlic dumplings I had packed at 6:40 a.m. I was twenty-eight, accounts payable, standing there with a plastic fork and a Diet Coke that had rolled to the back. "Maybe you forgot it at home," Brad said, already chewing something that looked exactly like my dumplings. I checked the Polaroid I had started taking of my lunch since Tuesday. Same blue lid. Same Sharpie heart. Brad's desk had a faint garlic smell and a napkin with chili oil. I printed ten freezer labels that said PROPERTY OF ACCOUNTING — CAMERA 3. I stuck one on the remaining yogurt, one on the mustard, and one on Brad's mystery protein shake. He laughed. "There's no Camera 3." I smiled like I agreed. At 12:41 the building Slack pinged: Facilities had posted a still from the hallway cam. A man in a grey polo was leaving the kitchen with a blue lid. Then Brad's shake started beeping because I had also stuck a timer label set for his 1 p.m. stand-up.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The Slack still is public; his shake timer is about to go off in a room full of managers.

social.video_title: He ate my dumplings on camera — Part 1/2
social.description: Office fridge, missing dumplings, and a coworker who swore Camera 3 didn't exist. I labeled everything anyway. Would you have posted the still?

parts.text: The timer chirped during stand-up. Brad jumped so hard his protein shake left a purple ring on the conference table. I forwarded the Slack still to the thread titled Kitchen Courtesy. "Blue lid, 12:11 p.m., grey polo," I typed. Our director asked if anyone wanted to discuss it. Brad said it was a misunderstanding and that leftovers were communal. I held up the Polaroid. "These were not leftovers. I packed them at 6:40." Facilities confirmed Camera 3 was the hallway unit nobody remembered because it only stored seventy-two hours. Brad offered to Venmo me nine dollars. I asked him to replace the Tupperware, the dumplings, and the hour I spent hungry on a closing deadline. HR called it a culture conversation. The fridge now has a sign: LABEL YOUR FOOD. DO NOT EAT LABELED FOOD. Brad brown-bags a sad turkey sandwich and eats it at his desk. I eat garlic dumplings in the kitchen with the door open.

social.video_title: The shake timer went off in stand-up — Part 2/2
social.description: Camera 3 existed. The Polaroid existed. His protein shake sang in a room full of managers. Was leftover ever a defense?
